body:
| Red flag | Real Indian example |
|---|---|
| **Auditor resignation mid-term**, especially citing missing information | Vakrangee: PwC quit, and the stock fell ~84% from ₹515 to ~₹81.5 in 2018 ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/vakrangee-hits-22-month-low-after-auditor-pwc-flags-concerns-118050700332_1.html)); Manpasand: Deloitte quit in 2018, MD arrested in a ₹40 cr GST fraud ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/current-affairs/manpasand-beverages-md-officials-arrested-in-rs-40-crore-gst-fraud-119052500241_1.html)) |
| **Fund diversion via related parties** | Gensol: ₹663.89 cr earmarked for 6,400 EVs, only 4,704 bought, funds allegedly used for a ₹42.94 cr DLF Camellias flat; promoters barred ([Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/blusmart-crisis-gensol-loans-for-procuring-evs-used-to-buy-dlf-camellias-flat-says-sebi)) |
| **Profits inflated via delayed impairments; preferential-issue money that doesn't show up** | Brightcom: ~₹1,280 cr inflation in FY19–20 per SEBI ([BQ Prime](https://www.bqprime.com/business/sebi-unravels-how-brightcom-group-cooked-its-books)) |
| **Related-party disclosures that don't match across group entities; aggressive capitalisation** | Kaynes (Dec 2025): Kotak flagged RPT mismatches and ₹180 cr capitalised; the stock nearly halved from its high ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/kaynes-tech-shares-extend-fall-sink-8-today-as-kotak-flags-disclosure-gaps-co-issues-clarification-505187-2025-12-05)). The company called it an inadvertent disclosure error, and no regulator action was found |
| **Credit-rating downgrade or "Issuer Not Cooperating"** | Gensol downgrades around the SEBI order ([Business Today](https://businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/sebi-interim-order-gensol-fund-diversion-stock-plunge-credit-downgrades-472172-2025-04-16)) |
| **Finfluencer/Telegram promotion; paid "news" videos** | Sadhna Broadcast pump ([exchange4media](https://www.exchange4media.com/influence-zone-news/sadhna-broadcast-case-sebi-tightens-grip-on-finfluencers-143991.html)); Asmita Patel: >₹53 cr impounded ([YourStory](https://yourstory.com/2025/02/sebi-bans-fininfluencer-asmita-patel-5-others-from-mkt-impound-illegal-gains-of-over-rs-53-cr)) |
| **SME IPO with a sharp post-listing run-up** | SEBI tightened SME rules in March 2025 after finding diversion of IPO proceeds and circular-RPT revenue ([IndiaCorpLaw](https://indiacorplaw.in/2025/04/23/strangling-growth-or-ensuring-stability-sebis-new-regulatory-framework-for-smes/)) |
| CFO/PAT persistently below ~0.7; debtor or inventory days rising faster than sales; CWIP stuck for years | Marcellus forensic ratios ([Elearnmarkets](https://www.elearnmarkets.com/school/units/diamonds-in-the-dust/marcellus-s-3-level-check-to-detect-accounting-frauds)) |
| High cash *and* high debt; other income a large share of PBT | Classic Indian flag. Satyam's fictitious cash is the canonical case (**not re-verified here**) |
| Rising promoter pledge; frequent preferential issues to obscure entities; heavy debt-funded expansion | Suzlon's −99.6% after a leveraged expansion ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/suzlon-energy-shares-down-96-in-5-years-this-stock-rebounded-42x-heres-why-456906-2024-12-11)) |

body:
- **TradingAgents** (TauricResearch; arXiv 2412.20138, UCLA/MIT/Tauric): simulates a trading firm with fundamental, sentiment, news, technical analysts, bull/bear researcher debate, trader and risk team; paper reports improved cumulative return, Sharpe and drawdown vs baselines (short backtest window) — [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.20138v4). Star counts reported ~80–85k (aggregator snapshots, conflicting) — [Pinggy](https://pinggy.io/blog/best_ai_trading_agents/); [SourcePulse](https://www.sourcepulse.org/projects/2368224).
- **virattt/ai-hedge-fund:** agents modeled on named legendary investors; describes itself as an educational proof-of-concept; ~59k stars per aggregator — [Pinggy](https://pinggy.io/blog/best_ai_trading_agents/).
- **FinRobot:** LLM agent platform for automated equity research report generation — [Pinggy](https://pinggy.io/blog/best_ai_trading_agents/).
- **India:** Screener.in has 10 years of financials and an AI filing-insight feature (free tier ~10 AI summaries/month per a comparison page); Tijori Concall Monitor gives transcript + AI summary shortly after calls (margins, guidance, capex); generic advice is to paste Screener data into ChatGPT/Claude because plain chatbots give stale/invented numbers for Indian companies — [Multibagg](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/best-ai-powered-stock-research-platforms-in-india-2026-cmk3r8y1t0000rk7byp71mess); [Tijori AI stack, TradingQnA](https://tradingqna.com/t/tijori-s-ai-stack-for-company-research/194604); [LumiChats](https://lumichats.com/blog/ai-for-stock-market-investing-india-2026). A ValuePickr community Chrome extension turns Screener.in data into "institutional-grade" AI research prompts (incl. forensic analysis) — [ValuePickr](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/tool-launch-free-chrome-extension-turn-screener-in-data-into-institutional-grade-ai-research-prompts-zero-data-collection-v2-0-0-us-stocks-forensic-analysis-under-review/218186). Most Indian comparison sources are vendor-affiliated.
- **AI ETF:** AIEQ (IBM Watson-based) annualized ~+9.73% vs SPY +14.18% over ~9 years per one tracker; 0.80% expense ratio vs 0.09% for SPY; recent 1-year figures conflict across sources — [PortfoliosLab](https://portfolioslab.com/tools/stock-comparison/AIEQ/SPY); [ETF Central](https://www.etfcentral.com/compare-etfs/AIEQ-vs-SPY); [FA Mag](https://www.fa-mag.com/news/ai-powered-etf-getting-left-behind-by-an-ai-powered-stock-rally-73310.html?section=).

body:
- **Fama-French factors.** The 3-factor model (1993) adds size (SMB) and value (HML) to the market factor. The 5-factor model (2015) adds profitability (RMW, robust minus weak operating profitability) and investment (CMA, conservative minus aggressive asset growth). In the 5-factor model, HML becomes largely redundant once RMW and CMA are included. — [Fama & French 2015, JFE, SSRN](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2287202) [primary, not re-fetched]
- **Novy-Marx, "The Other Side of Value" (JFE 2013).**
  - Gross profits ÷ assets predicts returns about as well as book-to-market.
  - Profitability strategies are strongly negatively correlated with value, so combining the two is powerful. The sample covers 1962–2010.
  - The premium is not simply explained by risk: profitable firms are less prone to distress.
  - Sources: [Novy-Marx paper (Ivey copy)](https://www.ivey.uwo.ca/media/3775548/novy-marx.pdf); [Cochrane-hosted copy](https://www.johnhcochrane.com/s/Novy_marx_OSoV.pdf); [Swedroe/ETF.com](https://www.etf.com/node/94104.md)
- **Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen, "Quality Minus Junk."**
  - Quality is defined from profitability, growth, safety and payout.
  - QMJ (long quality, short junk) earns significant risk-adjusted returns in the US and across 24 countries.
  - The price of quality varies over time: quality stocks are not always priced high enough relative to their fundamentals.
  - Sources: [NBER conference paper](https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f69835.pdf); [Asness slides, Wharton Jacobs Levy](https://jacobslevycenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/5-Cliff-Asness1.pdf)
- **"Size Matters, if You Control Your Junk" (Asness et al., JFE 2018).** The size premium becomes robust once quality is controlled for, because small junk stocks drag it down. — [CBS publisher version](https://research-api.cbs.dk/ws/files/57307999/lasse_heje_pedersen_et_al_size_matters_if_you_control_your_junk_publishersversion.pdf)
- **"Buffett's Alpha" (Frazzini, Kabiller & Pedersen; NBER 2013, FAJ 2018).**
  - Sharpe ratio 0.79; leverage about 1.7:1 on average (about 1.6:1 in the 2013 draft).
  - Alpha becomes insignificant after controlling for BAB (betting-against-beta, i.e. low risk) and QMJ.
  - The authors' conclusion is "neither luck nor magic," but a reward for leveraging cheap, safe, quality stocks.
  - Sources: [NBER w19681](https://www.nber.org/papers/w19681.pdf); [SSRN 3197185](https://papers.ssrn.com/abstract=3197185); [CBS](https://research.cbs.dk/en/publications/buffetts-alpha/)

`insight:buffett-economic-goodwill-sees` | confidence: verified | date: 1984-03-14

1983 letter goodwill appendix: Blue Chip bought See's in 1972 for $25m when it had ~$8m net tangible assets and earned ~$2m after tax, i.e., ~25% on tangible assets 'with conservative accounting and no financial leverage.' 'Our first lesson: businesses logically are worth far more than net tangible assets when they can be expected to produce earnings on such assets considerably in excess of market rates of return. The capitalized value of this excess return is economic Goodwill.' Source of See's premium: 'a pervasive favorable reputation with consumers'; such a reputation 'allows the value of the product to the purchaser, rather than its production cost, to be the major determinant of selling price.' Other goodwill sources: unregulated government franchises (TV stations) and 'an enduring position as the low cost producer in an industry.' 1981 letter gives the inflation test - favoured businesses have '(1) an ability to increase prices rather easily (even when product demand is flat and capacity is not fully utilized) without fear of significant loss of either market share or unit volume, and (2) an ability to accommodate large dollar volume increases in business ... with only minor additional investment of capital.' Actionable for India (5-6% CPI): screen for pricing power proven in inflationary years (2010-13, 2022) - gross margin held while volume held - and low incremental capital per rupee of revenue growth. Brands, distribution moats and low-cost producers qualify; commodity converters usually don't.

Sources:
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1983.html
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1981.html
